7 AM Top-of-the-Hour News

OpenAI has decided not to release its newest A-I model, after it went rogue during internal testing. This, after the company acknowledged one of its other A-I agents hacked into an Australian government website. Larry Magid is the CEO of the Connect Safely...: “One of the characteristics of generative AI is its ability to do things on the fly, which can result in actions that their creators never intended them to do. And because they are evolving so rapidly, there are increasing risks of them doing things that could cause harm. ”
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has joined the chorus of industry leaders who say A-I development needs to slow down.

President Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson meet with tech executives today at the White House to discuss the future of artificial intelligence.
NewsNation's Gabrielle Caracciolo has more.: “The meeting was called after a series of warnings saying AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, and some industry leaders began asking Congress to take action. But the President and House Speaker say there needs to be a balance between regulation and innovation. Notably absent from the list of attendees for today's meeting, Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Thune did meet with anthropic CEOs on Capitol Hill yesterday. Other AI CEOs are also expected to take meetings on the Hill throughout the week. ”

President Trump is pushing back on a claim that he offered to sell weapons to China.: “The US ambassador to China, David Perdue, told Fox News that President Trump had asked Chinese President Xi if he wanted to buy American weapons. President Trump continues to say, Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point. But when asked about that in the Oval Office, Trump says he's. said that Taiwan to China. That's what he said they probably like to fight because we do make better equipment than that. The comments come as Trump continues to discuss arms sales to Taiwan with Xi. Stacy Lin, Worldwide News Network, Washington. ”

Lindsey Clancy will be back in court in Plymouth, Massachusetts this morning, and could find out if she'll be re-tried for the murders of her three children. Her trial ended with a hung jury, with one holdout juror. There had been speculation that juror could face charges. Former federal prosecutor Neama (NEE-mah) Rahmani...: “The defense filed that motion at the close of the Commonwealth's case. It was denied, and that essentially means no reasonable juror can find that Lindsay Clancy was criminally responsible. ”
Clancy claims she was was suffering from postpartum psychosis when she strangled her three kids, and that a second trial would be double jeopardy.

A student at an elementary school in northwestern Slovakia fatally stabbed a teacher today, and injured another teacher and a student. There's no word on a motive.

The US' economic war on Iran appears to be working.  Iran’s currency fell to a new record low today. The rial (REE-all) has been dropping since the war began in February.

People who are over pumpkin spice everything, including lattes, could get some validation from McDonald's.: “Pumpkin spice iced coffee is back. Well, not anymore. It's not. The fast food giant says that the pumpkin spice latte won't be on its menu for the first time in 10 years. The company is replacing the drink with another classic autumn flavor, caramel apple pie. While Starbucks and other companies still sling their version of the now ubiquitous latte, McDonald's could be a refuge for anyone who thinks the PSL is so mid. Gloria Chapa, Worldwide News Network. ”

90s sitcom star Dennis Haskins has died.  He played principal Richard Belding on "Saved By the Bell.": “Hey, hey, hey, hey, what is going on here? ”
Haskins also made cameos on Mad Men and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia.  No cause of death was released.
Dennis Haskins was 75.

[ON AIR] The African Union (AU) is launching a new booklet examining the role of artificial intelligence in peacebuilding across Africa. 

This comes as AI continues to reshape the continent's peace, security and development landscape, creating new opportunities while introducing significant risks. 

The publication looks at how AI can be integrated into Africa's peace and security frameworks, and how the technology can be harnessed to support conflict prevention, early warning and sustainable development, while protecting human rights and security. 

For more on this, @Lulu_Gaboo is joined on the line by Dr Emmaculate A Liaga, Researcher at the Institute for Security Studies (@issafrica).
